solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Matched level in light drama, backer having withdrawn

indicators.note: the level is placed in the middle of the shortened drama word
the backer is the back or final letter, which withdraws from the word

parts.note: a comedy is a light drama
par means level, as in 'on a par'

explanation.surface: Someone notes that two things were evenly matched in a light play once its financial backer pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backer' looks like a theatre investor pulling out of the show, but it means the word's back letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Things compared are set side by side and matched against each other, a close synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Brilliant rescue dog detailed to enter cricket club

indicators.note: the shortened dog's name goes into the pair of club letters
de-tailed, with its tail or last letter removed

parts.note: Lassie is the fictional collie famous for rescuing people

explanation.surface: A heroic dog, cut short, joins a cricket club and proves brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as 'described closely' but means losing the tail, so LASSIE becomes LASSI.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic performance or example is outstanding, so brilliant is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Horse carrying disease endlessly spread

indicators.note: the horse word holds the shortened disease word inside it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: the disease word loses its final letter

parts.note: a malady is an illness or disease

explanation.surface: A horse is carrying a disease that has spread without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like the verb describing the disease, but it is the noun: something spread on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is an orange preserve eaten as a spread on bread or toast.

clue.text: Song about stinker seen in rural idyll

indicators.note: the song word goes around the stinker, sitting about it

parts.note: an aria is a song, especially in opera
a cad is a rotter or stinker, a man who behaves badly

explanation.surface: A song tells of a scoundrel turning up in a pastoral paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia, a region of ancient Greece, became the poetic byword for an unspoiled pastoral paradise.

clue.text: Style shown in being short with the French

indicators.note: short means lacking its last letter here

parts.note: an entity is a being, a thing that exists
le is the French masculine form of 'the'

explanation.surface: Fashionable style shows in being brief, as the French are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' is a verb here: to style someone is to give them a name or title.
explanation.definitionFit: To style a person something, such as 'Lord', is to give them that title or name.

clue.text: Seated outside clubs, Hesse emptied small bag

indicators.note: the seated word sits outside the other letters

parts.note: sat means seated
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: emptied means the inner letters of the poet's name are taken out, leaving its outer ones

explanation.surface: Hermann Hesse, sitting at a card table with clubs, empties a little bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Hesse is the German novelist; emptied, the name leaves HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed packet or bag, often of sugar, shampoo or scent.

clue.text: One to support stocking revolutionary American poet

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the American abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the US navy
Stephen Spender was an English poet

explanation.surface: A rebel American poet is someone who backs the stocking of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking' looks like a verb about keeping goods, but it is the hosiery a garter holds up.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is the elastic strap with a clip that holds up a stocking.

clue.text: Husband tucking into liqueur that's got body

indicators.note: the husband abbreviation tucks itself into the liqueur

parts.note: cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A husband tucks into a liqueur that has a full body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' looks like a wine-taster's word for the liqueur, but it is the frame of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the frame or body of a vehicle on which its other parts are mounted.

clue.text: Agreement achieved with three tens, minus tips

indicators.note: the tips are the first and last letters of the run of three tens, which are dropped

parts.note: three tens written out are ten, ten, ten

explanation.surface: A deal is struck involving three tens, with something knocked off each end.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding or agreement between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Wicked deeds at or around large towns

indicators.note: around means turned around, so the word or is read backwards

parts.note: cities are large towns

explanation.surface: Evil acts are committed at or near big towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocities are acts of extreme cruelty, which wicked deeds describes.

clue.text: Poet relieved of diamonds getting payment in advance

indicators.note: the poet is relieved of, or loses, the diamonds letter

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A poet robbed of his diamonds is paid in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put up before the cards are dealt, so a payment made beforehand.

clue.text: Why logician won't accept chair is obvious

definitions.text: Why logician won't accept chair is obvious

parts.words: Why logician won't accept chair is obvious
parts.note: a chair is upright on its legs, so a logician scorns it for being on its feet against logic; the phrase also means 'is obvious'

explanation.surface: It is plain why a philosopher refuses to sit in a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the phrase literally: a chair is on its legs, opposed to logic, so the logician rejects it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is logical or self-evident is said to be obvious to any sensible thinker.

clue.text: Daily forced to cancel leader in ridiculous pretence

parts.note: a daily or char is a cleaning lady who comes in each day

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is cancelled

parts.note: made means forced, as in 'made him go'

explanation.surface: A cleaner is forced to call off a leader in an absurd sham.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily, in British usage, is a domestic cleaner, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a show put on that nobody believes.

clue.text: Researcher wanting this instruction to make tea?

parts.note: read as an instruction, the pieces say doctor, or rearrange, the letters A T E, which gives TEA

explanation.surface: A scientist seeks an instruction for brewing a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer split into DOCTOR and ATE becomes an order to rearrange ATE into TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A PhD student working on a thesis is a researcher seeking the higher degree of doctor.

clue.text: Headless corpse is sent back for certain journey

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a corpse is a body, and with 'is' contracted it becomes body's

indicators.note: sent back means the word for agreement is read backwards

parts.note: yes means certainly, for certain

explanation.surface: A decapitated body is returned home in a certain trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corpse is' must be read as body's, with the apostrophe giving the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Homer's epic of Odysseus's wanderings, the word means any long adventurous trip.

clue.text: Romanians on the rampage in small republic

indicators.note: a rampage scatters things wildly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Romanians run riot in a tiny state.
explanation.definitionFit: This microstate, landlocked within Italy, is one of the oldest and smallest republics in the world.

clue.text: Divine law associated with electoral system

indicators.note: the two pieces are joined side by side, the system letters coming first

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
an edict is a decree or law

explanation.surface: A sacred law is linked with a voting system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' reads as 'holy' but is the verb: to foresee.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to foresee or guess by intuition what will happen.

clue.text: Alligator is one regarding soft floor covering

parts.note: re means regarding or about
P is piano, the musical direction for soft
a tile is a piece of floor covering

explanation.surface: An alligator is something you might find on a soft floor rug.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is an example of the cold-blooded scaly creature class that includes crocodiles and snakes.

clue.text: Prepare without finishing and study in China

indicators.note: the word loses its finish, its last letter

parts.note: to dress is to prepare, as with a salad or a wound
a den is a study, a private room

explanation.surface: Getting ready without completing the job, and studying in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is porcelain, not the country, and Dresden is a German city famed for fine porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is fine porcelain from the region around the German city, so a kind of china.

clue.text: Country folk involved in operatic number

indicators.note: the folk word is involved in, or placed inside, the operatic number

parts.note: an aria is a solo number in an opera
men means folk, people

explanation.surface: Country people are taking part in a song from an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the South Caucasus.

clue.text: Long article about a provincial Greek

indicators.note: the longing word goes about the letter given by 'a'

parts.note: to ache is to long for
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A lengthy piece on a Greek from the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the article but is the verb: to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Achaea was a province of Greece, so a native of it is a Greek from that region.

clue.text: Wine stain unfortunately showing up

parts.note: to mar is to stain or spoil

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: A wine stain, regrettably, is showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily.

clue.text: After correction, smile, as lacking purpose

indicators.note: a correction rearranges what was wrong, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Once corrected, the smile seems pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something with no aim or goal drifts without direction.

clue.text: Nobleman to free bananas at this point stuck in tree

indicators.note: the other pieces are stuck in the tree word, between its opening and closing letters

parts.note: a palm is a tree

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: here means at this point

explanation.surface: A lord sets out to rescue some bananas stuck up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit up the tree but means crazy, signalling the shuffle of TO FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A British lord sitting in the upper house holds a hereditary or life title, making him a noble.

clue.text: Fortify, across the pond, a private thoroughfare

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier, America being across the Atlantic
RD is the abbreviation for road, a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: An American defends a private road.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to read 'a private thoroughfare' as one phrase, but 'a private' is the American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To gird is to brace or strengthen, as in 'gird one's loins' before a fight.

clue.text: One to quit troubled Dáil Eireann — that causes rush!

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the letter for one quits, leaving the parliament's name

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone resigns from a turbulent Irish parliament, causing excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil Éireann is the lower house of the Irish parliament; drop one I and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This hormone is released under stress and produces the familiar surge of excitement and energy.

clue.text: Irishman joins Anglicans for spirited meeting

parts.note: Sean is a common Irish man's name
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: An Irish man joins the Anglican church for a lively gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' looks like 'lively' but means involving spirits of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: At a seance people gather to try to contact the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Outrageous sort of animus

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A shocking kind of hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notorious and shocking, known for wickedness, can be called outrageous.
